# tokens: # Late type-name resolution — the canonical cascade (ADR-012 rule 4)
# A capitalised name resolves through ONE cascade: the registry's
# binding store (user types), then the LIVE builtin table, then the
# slash-path resolver (eng/go/resolve.go). These rows pin the two
# families the pre-cascade code broke: names of types registered after
# parser init (NUR059 — they arrive engine-side as plain Words, like
# user types), and bare type-name children of typed containers
# (NUR060 — nothing resolved them; user-typed children silently
# failed while parser-eager builtin children worked).
# §1 — late-registered builtin names in typed defs and inspect.
# Bytes/Date are registered from lang at package init, AFTER the
# parser snapshot froze — so `Bytes` here exercises exactly the path
# every type name takes once the parser is name-blind.
def b:Bytes (convert Bytes 'hi') b
note: typed def names a late-registered builtin (was: def_error "type annotation must be a type value")
